extracted.intended_audience: readers, students, and critics of literature and public speaking; writers interested in principles of oratory and poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Critical notes and evaluative principles for judging oratory (sermons/public speaking) and poetry/dramatic works, illustrated by close observations of Father Taylor, Shakespeare, and Robert Burns. Emphasizes qualities of delivery, feeling, subject-matter, national relevance, and poetic technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action in Oratory
rubrics_metrics.description: The old Demosthenean rule and requirement of "action, action, action," first in its inward and then (very moderate and restrain'd) its outward sense, was the quality that had leading fulfilment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize inward psychological/ethical movement (internal action, emotional/moral impetus) and then controlled outward expression. Too much outward show without inner action is insufficient. Example: Father Taylor's sermons fulfill this rule in both inward force and restrained outward delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity / Live Feeling over Rhetoric
rubrics_metrics.description: When Father Taylor preach'd or pray'd, the rhetoric and art, the mere words... seem'd altogether to disappear, and the _live feeling_ advanced upon you and seiz'd you with a power before unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate speeches and prayers by the presence of authentic, felt emotion that transcends polished phrasing. Anti-pattern: elegant but hollow rhetoric that fails to move. Scoring note: emotional authenticity can outweigh formal literary polish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extemporaneous Delivery / No Manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: There was no sign of any MS., or reading from notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A natural, un-read delivery (apparent extemporaneity) is a mark of mastery and can increase force and immediacy. It signals internal command of material. Not an absolute requirement, but worth credit when assessing oratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Relevant Imagery and Audience-Tailored Allusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Especially were all allusions to ships and the ocean and sailors' lives, of unrival'd power and life-likeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good speakers and writers tailor imagery and references to the audience's experience (e.g., seafaring imagery for sailors). Concrete, situation-appropriate images increase impact. Example: the mural of a ship in a gale augmenting the sermon for a seafaring congregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probing the Conscience / Moral Penetration
rubrics_metrics.description: Such impassion'd pleading--such human-harassing reproach... such probing to the very depths of that latent conscience and remorse which probably lie somewhere in the background of every life, every soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess moral seriousness and the capacity of a speech or prayer to elicit deep self-examination or remorse. Powerful oratory reaches latent conscience rather than merely instructing or entertaining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural Unsophisticated Eloquence vs Trained Elocution
rubrics_metrics.description: Talking of oratory, why is it that the unsophisticated practices often strike deeper than the train'd ones?... we need to clearly understand the distinction between oratory and elocution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish innate oratory (deep, spontaneous eloquence) from elocution (trained technique). Value the former for its penetrative power even when it lacks polish; treat excessive elocution as sometimes less affecting. Example: country exhorters or local speakers sometimes produce more definite results than highly trained speakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety and Richness of Persons and Themes (Shakespeare)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most distinctive poems... the inward and outward characteristics of Shakspere are his vast and rich variety of persons and themes, with his wondrous delineation of each and all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure dramatic/poetic greatness by the breadth and subtlety of character-portraiture and thematic range. High marks for works that display many fully realized persons and variety of motifs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity / Controlling Plan Across Works
rubrics_metrics.description: It is plain to me that... afterward developed and defined his plan... systematically enlarged it to majestic and mature proportions... it is impossible to grasp the whole cluster of those plays... without thinking of them as, in a free sense, the result of an _essentially controling plan_.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a body of work evidences an overarching, coherent design or program. A controlling plan that binds disparate pieces into a larger artistic project is a sign of artistic ambition and coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concealment and Layered Meaning as Poetic Trait
rubrics_metrics.description: That inexplicable element of every highest poetic nature which causes it to cover up and involve its real purpose and meanings in folded removes and far recesses... hiding the nest where common seekers may never find it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value works that embed meanings subtly and rewards deep, repeated study. The presence of concealed layers and indirectness can be an index of depth and genius. Anti-pattern: overly explicit works with no reserve of meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability to Democratic/American Purposes (Accessibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shakspere... stands entirely for the mighty esthetic sceptres of the past, not for the spiritual and democratic... The comedies... are altogether non-acceptable to America and Democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge literature on how well it serves democratic audiences: accessibility, relevance to popular life, and alignment with democratic ideals. Works that presuppose aristocratic tastes may be judged less fit for democratic societies. This is a contextual/audience-based criterion rather than absolute aesthetic condemnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Magnetism / Life-Verse Fusion (Burns)
rubrics_metrics.description: No poet on record so fully bequeaths his own personal magnetism... how one's verses, by time and reading, can so curiously fuse with the versifier's own life and death, and give final light and shade to all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit poets whose life and persona infuse their work, creating an integrated appeal; the autobiographical or biographical aura can intensify reception and lasting fascination. Example: Burns's personal misfortunes enhance the emotional reading of his songs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Dialect and Native Idiom
rubrics_metrics.description: His brightest hit is his use of the Scotch patois, so full of terms flavor'd like wild fruits or berries... Mark the native spice and untranslatable twang in the very names of his songs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the effective use of local dialects and native idioms as assets that lend authenticity, color, and unique voice. Dialect can be a core strength, not merely a quaint novelty. Anti-pattern: forcing dialect where it feels inauthentic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfinishedness / Rawness as Artistic Value
rubrics_metrics.description: The frequent crudeness, haste, deficiencies... in this odd-kind chiel such points hardly mar the rest... often something in the very neglect, unfinish, careless nudity, slovenly hiatus... that secretly pleases the soul more than the wrought and re-wrought polish of the most perfect verse?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow aesthetic value for unpolished or raw works when the roughness is consonant with spirit and authenticity. Do not penalize lack of finish when it contributes to veracity or energy. Scoring note: rawness may count positively when it matches subject/mood; negatively when it indicates mere sloppiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Melody vs Complexity / Spiritual Depth
rubrics_metrics.description: He gives melodies, and now and then the simplest and sweetest ones; but harmonies, complications, oratorios in words, never... He has, moreover, little or no spirituality. This last is his mortal flaw and defect, tried by highest standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate simple melodic charm from deeper harmonic complexity and spiritual depth. A poet may be praised for melodic immediacy but critiqued for lacking higher structural or spiritual ambitions. Use this to calibrate scope and durability of poetic achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-Matter and Elevation of Theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Burns poetizes the humor, riotous blood, sulks, amorous torments, fondness for the tavern... He attempts none of these themes [of Homer or Shakespeare]... Burns is not at all great for New World study... he is intuitive and affectionate, but gives no philosophy worth mentioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the thematic ambition and seriousness of subject-matter: epic, philosophical, and universal themes often rate higher for perceived 'greatness' than narrowly local, convivial, or comic topics. Consider audience and cultural context when weighing this criterion.
